title: POC Scoping - Private Networking & Data Residency - Innovamed
summary: Discovery/POC scoping to confirm Innovamed's private networking and data residency requirements for a 4-week POC. Discussed VPC peering vs PrivateLink, egress restrictions, KMS/ENCRYPTION, regional placements (us-east-1, eu-west-1), success criteria (latency, throughput, cost), workload sizing and benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: share network diagram, Redwood to provide security docs and POC runbook, schedule initial benchmark in 10 business days.
action_items: Sarah Gomez: Share current network diagram and VPC CIDR blocks (due: 2025-07-24)
Connor Lee: Send Redwood private deployment security pack (SOC2, ISO, network hardening) and POC runbook (due: 2025-07-25)
Rina Patel: Prepare benchmark config and sample load script for us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (due: 2025-07-28)
David Chen: Confirm egress port allowances and proxy requirements (due: 2025-07-24)
Priya Rao: Approve scope and sign POC SOW (due: 2025-07-30)
next_steps: Redwood to run initial 10k request benchmark in Innovamed VPC (targets: p99 <250ms for 512 tokens, sustained 50 req/s)
Customer to provide network access and a test IAM role for the POC host
Schedule kickoff call + VPC peering setup next week
Agree on success criteria and stop/rollback conditions
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Connor Lee (Redwood AE), Rina Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO - Innovamed), Sarah Gomez (Head of MLOps - Innovamed), David Chen (Security Engineer - Innovamed)

Summary: POC scoping focused on private networking (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), data residency across us-east-1 and eu-west-1, egress constraints, KMS control, and benchmark success criteria. Action items and timeline discussed.

[00:00] Connor Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - i'm Connor from Redwood, and with me is Rina, our SE, we'll run through the private networking POC scope.
[00:18] Priya Rao: Hi, thanks. we're mainly concerned about data never leaving our VPC, certs and key control, and timing — want to run a 4 week POC to validate perf.
[00:30] Rina Patel: Great, can you give us the primary success criteria? latency, throughput, any cost targets?
[00:40] Sarah Gomez: Primary is p99 latency under 250ms for 512 token generation for our interactive apps. Secondary is throughput — we expect bursts to 50 rps sustained for short periods, and average around 10 rps. Cost target is more internal, but we'd like to see <= $X per 1M tokens as a benchmarking baseline.
[01:05] David Chen: Security wise we need customer-managed KMS, audit logs retained for 90 days, and we can't allow outbound traffic to third-party endpoints except to Redwood endpoints over PrivateLink or peering. Egress is a big one; we have corporate proxy rules.
[01:30] Connor Lee: Totally. For Private deployments we support VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. Both keep traffic inside the customer's network — peering gives flat L3 connectivity, PrivateLink gives interface endpoints and a little more control over egress. There's tradeoffs on cross-region routing.
[01:55] Priya Rao: Cross-region is critical. We need EU data not to egress to US. So for EU customers we want infra in eu-west-1. Can Redwood support dual-region POCs?
[02:10] Rina Patel: Yes, we can spin POC instances in both us-east-1 and eu-west-1. For data residency we can pin model serving to region. During the POC we can route EU traffic to eu-west-1 endpoints. We'll need the network connectivity set up per region.
[02:35] Sarah Gomez: On the network side, we use shared services in a central VPC and have restrictive outbound rules. We'll need to know which subnets and ports to permit. Also whether Redwood needs IAM roles or a bastion host.
[02:50] Connor Lee: Typically we ask for either VPC peering with a designated subnet where our nodes are reachable, or PrivateLink where you create an interface endpoint and we push traffic through. For peering we suggest using non-overlapping CIDRs; for PrivateLink we just need your endpoint IDs and security group rules. We'll send a spec doc.
[03:18] David Chen: Any special ports? Also do you need NAT? We try to avoid NAT for egress control.
[03:28] Rina Patel: Minimal outbound: typically TLS 443 to Redwood control plane endpoints; for PrivateLink peering it's all internal, but the service-on-host still needs to reach our management plane — we can do it over the peering. If you have strict egress, we can also use a customer-hosted proxy inside the VPC.
[03:50] Priya Rao: KMS— we need to retain control of keys. How does Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
[03:58] Connor Lee: We support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest for Private deployments. You can supply key ARNs; for hosted we manage keys but for private installs you'll keep key control. We'll include KMS config in the runbook.
[04:15] Sarah Gomez: Let's talk sizing. We expect average request size near 350 tokens, peak 1024 tokens in some workflows. Concurrency: typical clients will have 20 concurrent connections, but for an initial POC we want to validate up to 50 concurrent to be safe.
[04:33] Rina Patel: Good detail. For model choice, are you evaluating smaller quantized models or full fp16? That affects throughput and latency.
[04:40] Priya Rao: We'll likely start with a 13B open model quantized to 4-bit for cost, maybe try fp16 as a comparison. The Silicon we're targeting is NVIDIA A10/A100 in your Dedicated, or equivalent in Private.
[04:58] Connor Lee: Noted. For benchmarking we'll collect tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and cost-per-token estimates. We'll also do tail-latency profiling with KV-cache warm vs cold start.
[05:12] Sarah Gomez: Cold start behavior is important — do you pre-warm KV caches?
[05:18] Rina Patel: We can stage a warm cache for the benchmark set so you see steady-state tail numbers. We'll also run cold start scenarios to capture worst-case.
[05:30] David Chen: On network routing, if we do peering and the Redwood nodes sit in our VPC, are logs and audit trails available to us? We need flow logs and access logs.
[05:42] Connor Lee: Yes, flow logs are in your control since it's your VPC. Our side can emit audit events to your configured S3 endpoint if you'd like, or we can stream logs into your Splunk/Datadog via approved endpoints. We'll document supported sinks.
[05:55] Priya Rao: Let's sketch the benchmark plan and timeline. We're aiming for a 4-week POC starting August 4th. Initial network setup next week, benchmarks week 2, validation week 3, wrap up and decision week 4. Is that realistic?
[06:12] Rina Patel: That's feasible. Proposed schedule: Week 0 (this week) — exchange network docs and SOW; Week 1 — network setup and infra provisioning; Week 2 — run 10k request benchmark and stress tests across regions; Week 3 — iterate on tuning (batching, quantization); Week 4 — final report and handoff.
[06:36] Sarah Gomez: For the 10k test what are target metrics? We want p99 <250ms for 512 tokens, sustained 50 rps for short bursts, and p50 <80ms. Also we want to measure cost per 1M tokens as baseline.
[06:50] Connor Lee: We'll aim for that. We'll provide a spreadsheet with measured p50/p95/p99 and cost estimates across model variants. Also note we'll test canary fallback — e.g., if Dedicated capacity is constrained we'll fall back to a compatible quantized variant. We'll log that behavior.
[07:05] David Chen: About egress constraints again — if our policy blocks outbound DNS or other lookups, does Redwood require external DNS?
[07:12] Rina Patel: We can be configured to use your VPC-provided DNS. For private installs we can work entirely with your internal DNS and internal registries. We'll confirm specifics in the networking spec.
[07:24] Priya Rao: Any compliance docs we can review? SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports?
[07:30] Connor Lee: Yes, we'll send the security pack including SOC2 Type II, ISO attestation, SBOM summary, and our standard penetration test executive summary. For private deployments we also provide configuration hardening guidelines.
[07:45] Sarah Gomez: Great. On purchasing and SOW, we'll need a slim SOW for the POC with clear acceptance criteria, liabilities, and data handling specifics.
[07:55] Connor Lee: We'll draft a POC SOW and include the acceptance criteria we discussed: p99 latency threshold, throughput, data residency compliance, and no data exfiltration.
[08:05] Rina Patel: For the actual benchmark run we propose two scenarios: 1) steady-state with warm cache, 2) bursty traffic with cold starts. We'll capture latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, network stats.
[08:20] Priya Rao: Ok, sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[08:25] Connor Lee: We need the network diagram, VPC CIDRs, security groups, and approval for the POC IAM role or cross-account role. Once we have that we can provision the POC infra.
[08:36] David Chen: We'll compile that and share by Friday. Also need to confirm the contact for our infra team to coordinate setup.
[08:42] Sarah Gomez: I'll be the primary for the MLOps side. David will handle security. Priya will sign-off on the SOW.
[08:50] Connor Lee: Perfect. Quick note on metrics collection — we'll push metrics to a read-only S3 bucket you control for the POC and provide a dashboard link. Is S3 acceptable?
[08:59] Sarah Gomez: Yes, read-only S3 is fine. We use Splunk internally but can ingest S3 output.
[09:06] Priya Rao: On region separation, if we route EU traffic to eu-west-1 can you guarantee model artifacts won't be replicated to us-east?
[09:14] Rina Patel: For the POC we can pin model artifacts and inference to the region and prevent cross-region replication. We'll document the artifact lifecycle.
[09:26] David Chen: Anything else on encryption in transit? We need mutual TLS for the control plane interactions.
[09:32] Connor Lee: We support mTLS for control plane endpoints for Private deployments. We'll include cert exchange steps in the runbook.
[09:40] Sarah Gomez: Great. Let's recap next steps and action items.
[09:44] Connor Lee: Recap: Innovamed to share network diagram and egress constraints by Friday; Redwood to send security pack and POC SOW by Friday; Redwood SE to prepare benchmark scripts for us-east-1 and eu-west-1; schedule kickoff next Wednesday to start peering/privateLink setup.
[10:05] Priya Rao: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[10:10] David Chen: No further Qs from security after we share specifics.
[10:14] Sarah Gomez: Thanks, we'll review the docs once received.
[10:18] Connor Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments and meeting minutes.

End of transcript.
